Vendored from https://github.com/Aytixel/kinect-one
Revision: 24c6dc0

Local changes are marked with `LOCAL PATCH` comments, and the complete diff
against that revision is in UPSTREAM.patch. Four files differ:

  src/lib.rs
      Re-export `Opened`. `Device<Opened>` is the type every caller has to name
      in order to hold an open device, but the port only re-exported the
      `Device` wrapper, leaving the state parameter unnameable outside the crate.

  src/processor/registration.rs
      Restore upstream libfreenect2's out-of-image bounds check in
      `fill_depth_to_color_map`. Upstream records -1 for a border pixel whose
      distortion lands outside the raw image, and writes depth 0 for it; the port
      dropped the check and indexed the frame directly, which panics on real
      frames. This is a genuine upstream bug, not a local preference.

  src/processor/depth/cpu.rs
      An additive `#[cfg(test)]` module only, proving the parallel decode is
      bit-exact against the sequential one. No functional change: an earlier
      attempt to reshape the decode's inner loops measured about 1% and was
      reverted rather than carried.

  src/lib.rs (second change)
      Also export `DepthProcessorParams`. The process parameters are the
      constants every decoder is built from -- the OpenCL processor passes them
      to its kernel build, and the WGSL port needs them for the same reason. The
      `settings` module is private, so without this the type cannot be named from
      outside the crate at all.

  src/processor/depth/opencl.rs
      Comment only, recording that the kernel global work size comes from
      `ProQue::dims` and is deliberately not set at the kernel builders. No code
      change. Kept because that path produces silent all-zero output when it
      fails, and the work size is the first thing one suspects.

UPSTREAM.patch resolves with `-p1` from a directory containing `src/`.

Regenerating it, or rebasing onto a newer upstream:

    git clone https://github.com/Aytixel/kinect-one /tmp/k1
    git -C /tmp/k1 checkout 24c6dc0
    mkdir -p /tmp/pg/a /tmp/pg/b
    cp -r /tmp/k1/src /tmp/pg/a/src                 # pristine
    cp -r <this-crate>/src /tmp/pg/b/src            # vendored, patched
    (cd /tmp/pg && diff -ruN a b) > UPSTREAM.patch

Checking that the vendored copy really is upstream plus only these changes:

    cp -r /tmp/k1/src /tmp/verify/src
    (cd /tmp/verify && patch -p1 < UPSTREAM.patch && diff -rq src <this-crate>/src)
